es.summary: Desorden en el que el sistema inmunitario ataca tejidos propios, produciendo inflamación crónica y daño orgánico.
key_points: Pérdida de tolerancia al propio antígeno
Producción de autoanticuerpos y citocinas inflamatorias

pathophysiology: Fallos en la tolerancia central y periférica generan linfocitos autoreactivos.
Los linfocitos B producen autoanticuerpos que forman complejos inmunes.
Los complejos activan complemento y citocinas, provocando inflamación tisular.
Daño progresivo de órganos según el antígeno objetivo.
risk_factors: Exposición a químicos, tabaco y radiación.
signs_symptoms: Fiebre baja, artralgias o dolor articular.
Erupciones cutáneas, pérdida de cabello o ictericia según órgano afectado.
Síntomas específicos del órgano (ej. disnea en lupus pulmonar).
diagnostics: Pruebas de autoanticuerpos: ANA, anti‑dsDNA, RF, anti‑CCP.
Estudios de función orgánica (enzimas hepáticas, creatinina, glucosa).
Biopsia de tejido cuando el diagnóstico es incierto.
treatment: Corticoides (prednisona) para control rápido de la inflamación.
AINEs para dolor articular y antiagregantes cuando sea necesario.
complications: Daño irreversible de órganos (riñón, pulmón, corazón).
Efectos adversos de fármacos: osteoporosis, hepatotoxicidad, neoplasias.
nursing_care: Evaluar signos vitales y nivel de dolor cada 4 h.
Monitorear laboratorio: hemograma, glucosa, función hepática y renal, electrolitos.
Observar signos de infección: fiebre, leucocitosis, secreciones.
Educar sobre la toma correcta de inmunosupresores y efectos secundarios.
Fomentar descanso y actividades de bajo impacto según tolerancia.
patient_teaching: Importancia de la adherencia al tratamiento y no suspender sin indicación.
Reconocer signos de recaída o infección y reportarlos inmediatamente.
Medidas de prevención: higiene de manos, evitar multitudes durante neutropenia.
Mantener una dieta balanceada rica en calcio y vitamina D.
No fumar y limitar consumo de alcohol.

evidenced_by: disminución de la energía al realizar actividades diarias
outcomes: Nivel de energía: paciente reporta 7/10 en escala de 0‑10 en 1 semana.
Capacidad para realizar ADL: paciente completa actividades básicas sin ayuda en 2 semanas.

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de energía y capacidad funcional cada turno
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar cambios y ajustar el plan de cuidados.

interventions.action: Planificar períodos de descanso y actividades de bajo esfuerzo
interventions.rationale: Reduce la demanda energética y previene agotamiento.

interventions.action: Promover una nutrición adecuada con proteínas y calorías suficientes
interventions.rationale: Mejora la reserva energética y la reparación tisular.

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de conservación de energía (sentarse al vestirse, dividir tareas)
interventions.rationale: Facilita la realización de ADL sin exacerbar la fatiga.

interventions.action: Monitorear efectos secundarios de corticoides que puedan contribuir a la fatiga
interventions.rationale: Identifica causas modificables del cansancio.

outcomes: No se presentan signos de infección durante la hospitalización.
Temperatura corporal se mantiene < 37.5 °C en 48 h.

interventions.action: Realizar vigilancia de temperatura y signos de infección cada 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detección temprana permite intervención oportuna.

interventions.action: Aplicar técnicas de asepsia al manipular vías invasivas
interventions.rationale: Reduce la exposición a patógenos.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre higiene de manos y evitar contacto con personas enfermas
interventions.rationale: Previene la transmisión de infecciones.

interventions.action: Evaluar recuento de leucocitos y neutrófilos diariamente
interventions.rationale: Monitorea la inmunosupresión y riesgo infeccioso.

interventions.action: Administrar vacunas inactivas según calendario y protocolos institucionales
interventions.rationale: Proporciona protección sin riesgo de infección activa.

en.summary: A disorder in which the immune system attacks the body's own tissues, producing chronic inflammation and organ damage.
key_points: Production of autoantibodies and inflammatory cytokines

pathophysiology: Failures in central and peripheral tolerance generate autoreactive lymphocytes.
B lymphocytes produce autoantibodies that form immune complexes.
The complexes activate complement and cytokines, causing tissue inflammation.
Progressive organ damage occurs according to the target antigen.
risk_factors: Exposure to chemicals, tobacco, and radiation.
signs_symptoms: Low-grade fever, arthralgia or joint pain.
Skin rashes, hair loss or jaundice depending on affected organ.
Organ-specific symptoms (e.g., dyspnea in pulmonary lupus).
diagnostics: Autoantibody tests: ANA, anti‑dsDNA, RF, anti‑CCP.
Organ function studies (liver enzymes, creatinine, glucose).
Tissue biopsy when diagnosis is uncertain.
treatment: Immunosuppressive drugs: methotrexate, azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil.
NSAIDs for joint pain and antiplatelets when needed.
complications: Drug adverse effects: osteoporosis, hepatotoxicity, neoplasms.
nursing_care: Assess vital signs and pain level every 4 h.
Monitor labs: CBC, glucose, liver and kidney function, electrolytes.
Observe for signs of infection: fever, leukocytosis, secretions.
Educate on proper intake of immunosuppressants and side effects.
Encourage rest and low-impact activities as tolerated.
patient_teaching: Importance of medication adherence and not discontinuing without indication.
Recognize relapse or infection signs and report immediately.
Preventive measures: hand hygiene, avoid crowds during neutropenia.
Maintain a balanced diet rich in calcium and vitamin D.
Do not smoke and limit alcohol consumption.

outcomes: Energy level: patient reports 7/10 on 0‑10 scale in 1 week.
Ability to perform ADLs: patient completes basic activities without assistance in 2 weeks.

interventions.action: Assess energy level and functional capacity each shift
interventions.rationale: Detects changes and allows plan adjustment.

interventions.action: Plan rest periods and low-effort activities
interventions.rationale: Reduces energy demand and prevents exhaustion.

interventions.action: Promote adequate nutrition with sufficient protein and calories
interventions.rationale: Improves energy reserves and tissue repair.

interventions.action: Teach energy conservation techniques (sit while dressing, divide tasks)
interventions.rationale: Facilitates ADLs without exacerbating fatigue.

interventions.action: Monitor corticosteroid side effects that may contribute to fatigue
interventions.rationale: Identifies modifiable causes of tiredness.

outcomes: No signs of infection during hospitalization.

interventions.action: Monitor temperature and infection signs every 4 h
interventions.rationale: Early detection allows timely intervention.

interventions.action: Apply aseptic techniques when handling invasive lines
interventions.rationale: Reduces pathogen exposure.

interventions.action: Educate patient on hand hygiene and avoiding sick contacts
interventions.rationale: Prevents infection transmission.

interventions.action: Assess leukocyte and neutrophil counts daily
interventions.rationale: Monitors immunosuppression and infection risk.

interventions.action: Administer inactivated vaccines per schedule and institutional protocols
interventions.rationale: Provides protection without active infection risk.

sources.name: Pharmacology for Nurses: Introduction to the Inflammatory Response and Anti-inflammatory Drugs

summary.0.quote: With this disorder, the immune system attacks its own tissues, causing widespread inflammation and tissue damage affecting the joints, skin, kidneys, brain, lungs, and blood vessels.

key_points.0.quote: With autoimmunity , the immune system fails at this fundamental task; it mistakenly targets and attacks the body’s own healthy tissues, organs, and cells.

key_points.1.quote: This is thought to be due to an altered balance of the innate and acquired immune systems that leads to an overabundance of cytokines, chemokines, and autoantibodies that stimulate the activation of fibroblasts (Rosendahl et al., 2022).

key_points.2.quote: Genetic predisposition and environmental factors trigger an immune response that leads to neuronal cell death, nerve demyelination, and neuronal dysfunction.

key_points.3.quote: Biologic drugs such as adalimumab, etanercept, infliximab, and rituximab are discussed in Immunosuppressants, Biologics, Monoclonal Antibodies, and Biosimilar Drugs .

sections.diagnostics.1.quote: Elevated levels of CRP or an accelerated ESR suggest the presence of inflammation in the body.

sections.diagnostics.3.quote: Biopsy: In some cases, a tissue sample may be obtained through a biopsy to determine the cause and severity of inflammation.

sections.treatment.0.quote: Your doctor may give you corticosteroids or other medicines to help you feel better.

sections.complications.2.quote: Adverse Effects Deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary emboli Hypotension Hyperglycemia Optic neuropathy Pancreatitis Anemia Hepatoxicity Osteoporosis Alopec

sections.complications.3.quote: Common adverse effects for non-biologic DMARDs include nausea/vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, hepatotoxicity, rash, anemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, photosensitivity, elevated blood pressure, hair loss, hypotension, pancreatitis, and with methotrexate, optic neuritis.

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: Educate the client about the drug’s purpose, potential side effects, and benefits to help the client make an informed decision about the treatment plan.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Consistent adherence to the medication regimen helps control uric acid levels and prevent gout attacks.
